newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Rexam sell-off sooner not later.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Rexam sell-off sooner not later.

text.p: Rexam chief executive Rolf Borjesson said on Wednesday those businesses designated for disposal would be sold "sooner rather than later", but he declined to give an exact time frame.
"It will be sooner rather than later, but there is no time scale," he told Reuters in an interview. "The most important thing is that we do a proper job."

The industrial materials and packaging group earlier said it had designated a number of businesses for sale with a combined annual turnover of 303 million stg, operating assets of 161 million and an annual operating loss of two million.
Borjesson said he did not exclude the possibility of further sell-offs as part of the group's restructuring plan, first announced in September.
"This does not exclude that later on we should come to the conclusion that one or two others should be sold as well. But we have no other businesses in mind for the moment," he said.
Borjesson declined to comment on whether there were any potential buyers for the units at present. "I don't want to have any speculation on that," he said.
"We are going to sell these businesses so each gets a better parent. We will deal individually with each business."

The units designated for sale span several sectors -- food and beverages, industrial, beauty, packaging, printing, coated films and paper. Rexam said healthcare and building and engineering were not affected by the disposal plan.
Borjesson declined to comment on the amount of the likely proceeds from the disposals or what the money would be used for.
The planned sell-offs will allow Rexam to restructure into seven sectors, each with a clear market focus.

Borjesson said the group had no plans at present to add to these core sectors. "We don't have any current plans, but I would be very surprised if we don't add businesses to these sectors in the future," he said.
